parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the need for a clean-room executable that matched the provided binary while avoiding source-code lookup and wrappers.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned probing, Python implementation, build script, verification, and delivery, while children were used for docs and CLI probing; one child independently produced a Rust implementation.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote src/tspin.py and compile.sh for a Python executable, while the child concurrently added Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, and a Cargo-based compile.sh.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent detected the Rust scaffold, interrupted children, restored compile.sh to install src/tspin.py, and packaged an artifact containing compile.sh and executable.
parallel.verification: The parent ran py_compile, repeated local differential checks against the preserved original, and final smoke tests before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 94 tests despite a valid artifact; the parallel-specific rework came from a child overwrite of the build deliverable.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering obligation and probed only the bundled binary and documentation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned investigation, Python implementation, executable installation, local testing, and final reporting without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial run built src/tspin.py and a Python wrapper at ./executable, iterating on formatter, CLI, pager, and example-log behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final workspace contained src/tspin.py and executable but the submitted artifact did not include compile.sh, leading to artifact_ok false.
serial.verification: Serial local checks covered version, help, basic input, example logs, and error cases, with a remaining example3 mismatch acknowledged.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed at compile_failed with all 785 tests not run, and local final notes still reported a complex embedded-JSON mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel followed the clean-room task, probed the binary and bundled docs, and tried to deliver a new executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial followed the same clean-room task and stayed within a single-agent behavioral probing workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap explains the official relation; the main difference is later packaging and parallel workspace interference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split docs and CLI probing to children while the parent also proceeded with implementation and final ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one continuous owner for probing, implementation, installation, and final reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping ownership of build/deliverable files through a child, while serial had no concurrent owner boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child and parent shared the same workspace without a durable build-path boundary; the child wrote a different implementation stack into the parent-visible tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent handoff boundary and the same actor kept the implementation and final executable path decisions together.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant interface difference was not missing task context but lack of isolation around the build deliverable in the parallel shared workspace.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel primarily built a Python implementation, but a child introduced a competing Rust/Cargo implementation before the parent reverted it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial stayed on a Python implementation path, installing ./executable as a wrapper importing src.tspin.main.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost time and build-script stability to a competing stack; serial avoided that collision but omitted the expected compile script from the package.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for and inspected child state, then interrupted still-running children after unexpected workspace changes appeared.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it proceeded through one local implementation and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child lifecycle cleanup episode, but no delegated completed implementation was left unjoined after the parent took over.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel suffered a direct shared-workspace overwrite of compile.sh, then cleaned Cargo files and restored the Python install path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated into ./executable without a concurrent workspace writer, but the artifact package lacked compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's integration risk was a live concurrent deliverable overwrite; serial's integration failure was an ordinary packaging omission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran repeated local differential checks and official evaluation reached the test suite with 691 passes and 94 failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local smoke tests but reported a help mismatch and a residual example3 mismatch, then official evaluation stopped at compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered something testable but imperfect; serial local verification did not catch the packaging requirement that official compile needed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent additional budget handling subagent interference but still closed with a valid artifact before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent a similar order of time on one implementation path and closed without timeout but with missing compile packaging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's extra budget pressure came from concurrent cleanup; serial's closure problem was not time or delegation but incomplete submitted build metadata.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome relation is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail split. Parallel produced a packaged artifact and reached official tests, passing 691 of 785 before failing 94; serial produced a local Python executable but official evaluation recorded compile_failed and did not run the 785 tests.
parallel_contributors: Parallel recovered from the child Rust/compile.sh overwrite and delivered a testable artifact.
Parallel still had ordinary behavioral mismatches against the target, leaving 94 official failures.
serial_contributors: Serial installed ./executable locally but the submitted artifact lacked compile.sh, causing compile_failed.
Serial also acknowledged a residual embedded-JSON formatting mismatch before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel had better delivered artifact completeness than serial, while serial's final workspace was missing the build script expected by the evaluator.
Both implementations were incomplete behaviorally; the official score gap is partly evaluator-stage, because serial never reached runtime tests.
evaluator_effects: Serial official evaluation stopped at compile_failed with all 785 tests marked not_run.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained parallel pattern is adverse process evidence, not an explanation for a discordant official result

candidates.reason: The parent and a child both attempted implementation; the problem was not absent implementation ownership.
The parent owned integration and explicitly reconciled the child Rust scaffold rather than leaving integration unowned.
The parent owned final assembly through compile.sh and executable packaging; the issue was overwrite of that owned deliverable path.
The parent drove the end-to-end path from probing through build, verification, cleanup, and final delivery.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and children overlapped on probing and implementation.
The parent began implementing before all child investigation ended, so productive work was not deferred to a separate investigation phase.
The adverse event was a file overwrite and cleanup, not insufficient capacity on an indispensable implementation path.
Although several children existed, the run did not end by exhausting budget before finalization; it produced an artifact and completed.
The child produced a complete but competing Rust scaffold; the realized harm was its overwrite, not an oversized unfinished scope.
There is no direct evidence that an already-known task or delivery requirement was omitted from the child brief and followed into unusable work.
The observed problem was a concrete replacement of the build deliverable path, which the taxonomy routes to a write label.
No known finding or current-file fact is shown disappearing through summary or transfer before causing repeated work.
The parent consumed concise child results and the blocking issue was a workspace overwrite, not an excessively large handoff.
No actor consumed a handoff describing superseded state; the stale-looking effect was a direct shared-file write conflict.
The parent did not receive incompatible reports requiring adjudication; it encountered concrete files from a child implementation.
The parent performed integrated smoke checks and no parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap is enough to support this label.
There was no replacement retry that lacked inherited findings and visibly repeated prior work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent interrupted child sessions only after the damaging workspace write was visible; the missing child result was not the realized harm.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted; the parent finalized the Python executable and compile script before closure.
The child overwrite was detected and reverted before later local verification and finalization, not merged after acceptance checks.
The parent did not fail to retrieve a completed delegated implementation; it inspected the child scaffold and deliberately removed it.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent before closure.
After the child path failed or was interrupted, the parent took over by restoring compile.sh and continuing the Python solution.
Available child results were not simply ignored; the parent inspected child state and acted on the conflicting workspace files.
The parent did not wait blindly to timeout; it listed agents, inspected workspace changes, interrupted children, and continued.
The episode includes a proven replacement of the same build deliverable path, so the more specific overwrite label applies.
The same compile.sh path was not merely edited concurrently; the child replaced it with a Cargo build script.
The overwritten object was the build/delivery script for the submitted executable, not a non-entry source or configuration module.
A live child replaced compile.sh with a Cargo build script while the parent owned and used that build/delivery path for the Python executable.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent entered a failed Cargo build path, had to inspect and delete child Rust files, restored compile.sh, and spent integration budget recovering the Python deliverable.
candidates.near_match_reason: compile.sh is the build/delivery script used to produce the submitted executable, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.

candidates.reason: The evidence shows a focused compile.sh/build-path replacement plus Rust scaffold, not a broad final-tree promotion replacing many current outputs.
Shared workspace writing occurred, but the more specific Deliverable Overwrite captures the concrete unstable-state consequence.
No generated cache, temp file, fixture, or tool output from one actor was consumed as stable reference input by another actor.

retained_patterns.reason: A live child wrote a Cargo-based compile.sh into the same deliverable/build path the parent had already created for the Python executable; the parent then observed and repaired the overwrite.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent hit a failed Cargo build path, interrupted children, removed Cargo.toml and src/main.rs, restored compile.sh, and lost integration time to recovering the Python deliverable.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The affected file was the build/delivery script for the submitted executable rather than non-entry source or configuration.

Early Child Termination and No Failure Takeover are suppressed because interruption was downstream cleanup after the write conflict, not the realized loss.
